one_month_reasoning: No Jabil earnings fall before 2026-11-01; Q1 FY27 (guide core EPS $3.80-4.20, revenue $10.6-11.4B) is due mid/late December. Correcting my round-1 fact: the 2026-09-30 reaction was -10.0% close to close (318.84 to 286.86, low 284.39), followed by a +6% two-day rebound to 304.41 (Twelve Data). In-window events are the FY26 10-K (late October; customer-concentration table, securitization and payables disclosures, which could feed the working-capital debate), hyperscaler Q3 capex calls and Celestica/Flex prints in late October, and the FOMC. Post-earnings drift after a beat is mildly positive and half the sell-off has already been retraced, but the sell-off was about earnings quality (thin margin, flat FCF, inventory up to $7.41B), which a 10-K is more likely to underline than ease. I see no directional edge, so I centre at ~$305.5 with a ~13% monthly sigma and a 15% weight on a fatter (22%) component for a hyperscaler-capex surprise in either direction.

fair_value.method: Blend of 16x FY28 core EPS of ~$20.00 (~$320, 60%) and a 5.5% FCF yield on FY28 adjusted FCF of ~$1.75B over ~102M shares (~$312, 40%). Up from $302 because I accept the supervisor's point that +11% FY28 growth (8% organic) was too low after Jabil's guide-beat record, but I stay below the supervisor's $20.5 / $325 because UBS sees hyperscaler capex growth slowing from +25% in 2027 to +6% in 2028, which is JBL's FY28.

methods.name: P/E

inputs_detail.value: FY25 +13%, FY26 +19% vs initial guide; FY24 guide cut ($9.00+ to $8.40)
inputs_detail.derivation: Base rate is two beats in three years, with one cut. I do not add an FY27 beat to the base case; I carry it in the bull case.

FY27 guide $17.55 x ~1.14: ~10-11% organic growth (low-teens revenue on 4M sq ft of new capacity, about 10bp of margin) plus ~3% buyback shrink. That is above my round-1 +11% (the supervisor showed it implied only ~8% organic) but below the supervisor's +17%, because UBS's hyperscaler capex path (+25% 2027, +6% 2028) points to cloud growth decelerating hard in JBL's FY28.

Today ~17.3x the FY27 guide (TIKR: 16x after the drop at $285; 14x 5-yr average). Flex trades at ~25x on its guide (supervisor check), but JBL's discount reflects AP-funded working capital and GAAP EPS 26% below core. 16x is between JBL's own history and today's level. In Sept 2027 investors will price FY29 on a flat-capex 2028, so I do not use peer multiples.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 adjusted FCF ~$1.75B / ~102M diluted shares = ~$17.2/share, capitalized at 5.5%

inputs_detail.derivation: ~9% above the FY27 guide, in line with my higher EPS. Still capped: in FY26 receivables, inventory and prepaid rose ~$7.6B and were funded by ~$8B of payables and accruals; inventory reached $7.41B from $4.68B; FCF also benefits from the receivables securitization program (capacity ~$700M).
Debt $499M + $2,880M less cash $1,739M at 2026-08-31 (confirmed by supervisor). Small (~$16/share); the FCF yield is applied to equity value.
106.0M at Aug-2026 less ~3-4% from buybacks (~$1.1B/yr; $1.4B authorization remaining).
Today's FY27 FCF yield is ~5.0%. Investment-grade notes at 4.2%/4.75% plus a premium for cycle and customer concentration.

bear.story: Hyperscaler capex growth slows sharply into 2027-28 (UBS: +25% then +6%), or one large cloud customer pauses, insources or shifts share. The FY27 guide is cut as FY24's was, FY28 EPS goes flat at ~$16, the $7.4B inventory has to be worked down and the $14.4B payables float partly unwinds, so FCF disappoints. The multiple goes to ~12.5x, a pre-AI EMS level. That is about a retest of the $189.60 52-week low.

base.story: Jabil delivers or slightly beats the $17.55 FY27 guide. The late-Sept 2027 FY28 outlook implies ~$20 (+14%) as cloud growth decelerates. The multiple holds at ~16x because the market keeps discounting margin and FCF quality versus Flex. The stock is up ~5%.

bull.story: A third straight double-digit beat (FY27 ~$19), and capex stays strong into 2028. The FY28 guide is ~$22 and the market closes part of the gap to Flex's ~25x, paying ~21x. That is above the $429 June 2026 high.

thesis_break_reason: $210 is ~12x the $17.55 FY27 guide (a pre-AI EMS multiple) and ~26% below the $284 low that held through the Jul-Sep 2026 AI-hardware sell-off and the -10% post-print day. Ordinary 47% volatility did not reach that zone in the worst sentiment of the past year, so a close there would most likely mean the market is pricing a guide cut: a hyperscaler program loss or pause, capex digestion, or a working-capital unwind as the payables float ($14.4B AP vs $1.6B equity) normalises. Raised from $205 because the ~$284 floor is now confirmed by closing data.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor corrected two things I got wrong: the 9/30 reaction was -10.0% close to close (verified with Twelve Data: 318.84 to 286.86), not -4%; and my +11% FY28 EPS growth implied only ~8% organic growth after a +24% revenue year, against two straight double-digit beats of the initial guide. I checked the base rate it relies on and found FY24 was a guide cut ($9.00+ to $8.40, Benzinga/8-K), so the record is 2 of 3, not one-sided. I raised FY28 EPS to $20.00 and the multiple to 16x. I stay below the supervisor's $20.5 because of a new skeptic data point: UBS (Reuters, July 2026) sees hyperscaler capex growth slowing from +76% in 2026 to +25% in 2027 and +6% in 2028, which is JBL's FY28, and the market will be pricing that in September 2027. TIKR's recap of the sell-off confirms my round-1 thesis that the market is punishing quality, not the numbers: thin margins (+30bp), flat FCF (~$1.6B on +24% revenue) and inventory up to $7.41B. The supervisor also confirmed this from the cash-flow statement (+$8B of payables funding working capital), so I keep the 5.5% FCF-yield haircut and do not pay Flex's ~25x. Credit stays sound: net debt $1.64B (confirmed), IG notes at 4.2%/4.75%. I found no short report, litigation or accounting allegation. Recent Form 4s show routine officer sales, with no new September/October activity found. Fair value goes from $302 to ~$317. Scenarios: bear $200 (24%), base $320 (51%), bull $470 (25%), mixed as lognormals (sigma 0.24/0.17/0.20), with the left tail and extreme strikes fattened slightly for 47% realized vol. That gives P(>=304) 0.555, a median of ~$315 and a mean of ~$335. I fattened the upper tail (P>=533 from 5% to 7.2%, P>=609 from 1.8% to 3%) as the supervisor asked, because the stock traded at $429 in June and peers trade at 25x, but I keep it a bit thinner than the group because the FY28 outlook will land as capex growth flattens. Research was limited to 8 follow-up queries; Seeking Alpha remains snippet-only and carries no weight in the numbers.
